absent: Locking rules for nested VMCB, MMU and bitmap access.
Full C layouts, sizes and offsets of VMCB and cached areas.
Numeric ABI values for intercepts, masks, vectors and MSRs.
Complete nested entry and exit state machine beyond shown prefix.
Behavior of TLB flush, PMU notification and guest mode transition.
Exported symbols; no export macros appear in fragments.

findings.text: When a Hyper-V vCPU record exists, nested state refresh copies partition assist address plus VM and VP identifiers from the enlightened control area into the nested Hyper-V record. L2 flush is considered enabled only when the nested flush control is set and the assist page advertises direct hypercall. A state counts as an L2 flush hypercall only when guest CPUID advertises L2 flush, the enable test passes, and the generic flush hypercall test passes.
In the disabled configuration the nested VM and VP identifier refresh does nothing, the L2 flush hypercall predicate is constantly false, and the synthetic exit injection after flush does nothing.

Nested page fault injection selects the fault stage from hardware exit information for hardware exits and from the fault error code otherwise, then normalizes to the final page annotation when the stage does not contain exactly one bit. It records a nested page fault exit with combined stage and remaining error bits plus fault address, then performs a nested exit.

Nested MMU setup points the active MMU at the guest MMU, builds a shadow nested paging MMU from L1 control register values and the cached nested CR3 with associated misc controls, and installs nested walk helpers for top level pointer retrieval, PDPTE fetch with low bits ignored for alignment, and page fault injection.

At init a small deduplicated table of permission bitmap chunk indices is built from a fixed MSR list covering system call, segment base, speculation control, performance and branch record groups. Each MSR is converted to a bit number, mapped to a word offset, deduplicated, and stored up to a capacity of ten entries, failing if a conversion is invalid or capacity is exceeded.
Permission bit calculation accepts three disjoint MSR windows distinguished by high bits and rejects others. Accepted values map linearly from range base plus masked offset scaled by bits per MSR.

Permission merge first honors a Hyper-V clean enlightenment fast path that can skip rereading and only refresh the effective base. Otherwise it does nothing unless L1 intercepts the protection MSR range. When merging, it reads each deduplicated chunk from L1 guest memory, combines with the host bitmap, clears the recalculation request, and publishes the merged bitmap base with memory encryption adjustment. A guest read failure aborts the entry preparation.

Bitmap base validation requires both the aligned start page and the final byte of the stated span to be legal guest addresses. Event injection with the valid flag clear is always accepted; otherwise the type must be interrupt, NMI, exception or software, and exception vectors are limited to defined architectural vectors with shadow stack and SEV-ES tied vectors gated on respective guest capabilities.

Cached control validation requires VMRUN interception, nonzero address space identifier, legal nested CR3 when nested paging is enabled, legal MSR and IO permission ranges, NMI virtualization only with NMI interception, and valid event injection. Cached save validation requires virtualization enable, coherent cache settings within 32 bits, valid debug registers, long mode coherence of paging, protection, address extension, legal CR3 and segment mode exclusivity, valid CR4 and EFER, and valid PAT when L2 uses a separate PAT. Combined failure is reported as invalid argument.

Copy from architectural control area to cache copies intercept words then clears feature gated intercepts for save restore, process context identifier, timestamp read, secure init and read protection register when the guest lacks them, masks misc enables for nested paging and translation enforcement, aligns permission bases, and masks TLB control, interrupt vector, shadow, exit and injection reserved bits. Save copy carries segments, descriptor tables, privilege level, feature, control and debug registers, flags, instruction and stack pointers, CET state, accumulator, fault address and PAT plus branch records. Hyper-V enlightenments are copied only when hypercalls are enabled.

Synchronization from the running VMCB refreshes pending injection and shadow state and merges only processor written interrupt bits. Virtual IRQ is withheld when the host has usurped the interrupt window intercept, while virtual GIF and NMI blocking and pending bits are included only when respective nested virtualizations are active. Nested NMI is active only when the guest supports it and L1 enabled it.

Second level save preparation detects a changed L1 VMCB address to force bitmap recalculation and full reload, otherwise refreshes segment, descriptor, CET and debug groups only when their clean bits indicate dirtiness, selects PAT from L1 or host according to separate PAT use, and loads flags, feature, control registers, fault address, accumulator, stack and instruction pointers into both vCPU state and fallback fields with fixed debug bits enforced and branch records sourced from L1 or host. Control preparation flushes TLB on transition, enters guest mode, notifies performance monitoring, splits interrupt masking between host and guest, propagates GIF and NMI controls when allowed, requeues pending host NMI as a request, and inherits nested paging mode and permission bases from the host VMCB.

An injection is software like when valid and either marked software or an exception whose vector is breakpoint or overflow; only those two vectors count as soft. An injection is NMI like when valid and marked NMI. A cached clean bit clear means the corresponding group is dirty. Setting the PAT value also marks the nested paging group dirty. Log messages are prefixed with the module name.

A failed guest PDPTE read yields zero without explicit error propagation, so callers must treat zero as failure. A failed L1 bitmap chunk read aborts merge and thus entry preparation. Malformed fault stage with zero or multiple bits is forced to final page annotation with a one time warning. Invalid cached control or save state fails entry rather than entering the guest.

Visible entry points observed are init of merge offsets at boot, cached VMCB validation, control and save copy helpers to cache, control synchronization from the running VMCB, and second level save preparation helpers. Hyper-V helpers are inline predicates and updates with no-op fallbacks.

Observed cached control grouping includes address space identifier and clean word, intercept words, permission base addresses, timestamp offset, TLB and interrupt controls, exit and injection fields, next instruction pointer, nested CR3, pause filter controls and optional enlightenment area. Observed cached save grouping includes privilege level, segments, descriptor tables, feature and control registers, debug registers, flags, instruction and stack pointers, CET state, accumulator, fault address, PAT and branch records.
Merge of permission bitmaps operates in units of native unsigned long words.
